Hi Liam / Priya —

Attached is the Q2 renewal health packet you asked for: a short exec summary, token mix breakdown, and a per-route latency/cost heatmap. TL;DR: overall consumption is up 42% QoQ driven by the new summarization pipeline (100–400 tokens/gen) and an increased rate of streaming responses. Performance has been stable, but the traffic shift increases our 99th-p90 tail exposure on the current m1-small cluster.

Key asks in the packet:
- Confirm whether peak concurrency (observed Novacorp-prod: ~420 concurrent requests at 120s window) is expected to continue into H2.
- Decide whether you want to: 1) keep current reserved capacity and add burst credits, or 2) move to a dedicated + autoscale pilot (+20% baseline, +50% burst).

Suggested next steps:
1) Internal ops pilot for a 2-week canary on dedicated nodes (can enable quantized variant for cost parity) — we can provision starting May 3.
2) If you opt for the dedicated pilot, we recommend a staged uplift to handle 1.5x current sustained throughput and a 2.0x burst corridor.
3) If you want a pricing/term change, Ben and Karthik can draft a short one-page amendment tied to throughput milestones.

I've included priya and liam on the thread — Priya, any immediate concerns from the product side? Liam, can you confirm whether the concurrency profile is expected to remain?

Thanks,
Sofia
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Thanks, Sofia — useful packet. Quick answers:
- Yes, the concurrency is expected to hold; May–Aug is our user acquisition window and we expect steady increases (estimate +30% sustained, +60% during promo spikes).
- The key risk for us is latency regressions during spikes; we cannot tolerate >200ms p95 regressions on search endpoints.

Questions:
1) For the dedicated pilot — what SLAs can you commit to for p95/p99 during the canary?
2) Can you show a cost comparison (current hosted vs dedicated pilot with quantization) over the next 3 months?
3) We have a procurement timeline (legal + finance) — is a one-page amendment workable to shorten procurement cycles?

— Liam

Liam — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers up front:
- SLA targets for the canary: p95 <= 150ms; p99 <= 400ms with automatic fallback to the lower-cost model if we breach for >5 consecutive minutes. We will enable tracing and synthetic checks across your top-20 routes.
- Cost comparison: attaching a one-page delta (see link in Drive). High level: dedicated + mixed-quantization is ~18% lower unit cost at 1.5x sustained throughput vs hosted, and ~12% lower at peak bursts when using burst credits.
- One-page amendment: yes — Ben and Karthik, can you draft a procurement-friendly amendment (term: add dedicated pilot, 90-day evaluation, milestone-based capacity uplift) and include a simple cancellation clause? Procurement wants minimal gating.

Operational plan (proposed):
1) Provision a 2-week dedicated pilot starting May 3 (redwood ops) — will mirror production routing and enable continuous batching and KV prefix caching for your summarization routes.
2) Week 0–1: run dry-run synthetic traffic (our test harness) to tune kernel selection and quantization knobs.
3) Week 1–2: enable live traffic at 20% and ramp to 50% if latency targets hold.
4) Onpass: If p95/p99 breaches, auto-fallback and rollback within 10 minutes; we'll run retrospective and recommend model/infra adjustments.

Ben / Karthik / Naomi — please coordinate the amendment and the pricing delta; include a 30% cap on any uplift price change during the pilot for predictability (Liam: that was a procurement ask yesterday). Liam — is May 3–17 workable for the pilot window on your side?

Best,
Sofia
